COMMON JUDGMENT The Petitioners have filed these petitions under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act seeking Channakeshava.K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110324970/ 2 Compensation for the death of one M.Madhu and for the injuries suffered by the petitioners in MVC No.842/2023 & MVC No.1499/2023 in an RTA on 23.01.2023. All the petitions arose out of a common accident, therefore all the petitions are clubbed together as per order dated 16.01.2024 and common evidence is recorded and common Judgment is passed. SCCH - 25 4 MVC Nos.836/2023 842/2023 & 1499/2023 2. When they were passing near Thippadoddi Cross, at Narayanaswamy House on Bangalore - Chennai NH Road, Gangavaram Mandalam, Palamaner Taluk, Chittoor District (A.P.), a Mahindra Pickup Goods carriage vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-TT-3260 came with high speed from the back side i.e., Bangalore side to go to Chennai side, the driver of the said vehicle drove it with over speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle in which deceased M.Madhu and B.Anji and Chenna Keshava's were going, as a result the rider of the Two wheeler Chenna SCCH - 25 5 MVC Nos.836/2023 842/2023 & 1499/2023 Channakeshava. K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110324970/ 3 From whom? 3. What order or Award? Channakeshava On perusal of documents it is clear that the accident occurred on 23.01.2023 at about 18.20 and the FIR was registered on the next day at about 9.00am. The complaint was given by Venkatesh M. Father of deceased M.Madhu. The Sketch shows that the accident occurred on the NH of Bangalore - Chittoor. The Inquest Mahazar conducted on 21.01.2023 from 10.00am to 24.01.2023 Channakeshava. K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 (ii) (2009) 13 Supreme Court Cases 654 : Raja Rani and Ors. Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., and Ors.
texts.facts: Keshava and pillion riders M.Madhu and B.Anji fell down on the Road, sustained grievous injuries. The 1st Respondent being the RC owner and 2nd respondent being SCCH - 25 8 MVC Nos.836/2023 842/2023 & 1499/2023 the insurer of the offending Mahindra Pickup Goods Carriage vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners. The accident was caused solely due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.AP-39- Channakeshava.K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110324970/ 6 RN-7194. Further contended that the TWO WHEELER IS DESIGNED FOR TWO PERSONS ONLY AND NOT FOR TOO MANY PERSONS. There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) of MV Act. The rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-RN-7194 did not have valid DL as on the date of accident, he rode the two wheeler motorcycle with 2 pillion riders in utter violation of the traffic Rules and also the provisions of the MV Act and Rules. were not wearing the helmet at the time of accident. Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate. The respondent did not prove their defence. The petitioner in MVC No.842/2023 have claimed for a sum of Rs.30,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.12,59,000/- with interest @6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
texts.arguments: The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.
